method.text: يجب الحضور شخصيًا إلى السفارة أو القنصلية التونسية ببلد الإقامة، لتقديم طلب التأشيرة، وشرح أسباب السفر وظروفه.

passportValidity.text: The UK FCDO says your passport should be valid for the duration of your stay and in good condition: travellers who enter with a damaged or torn passport may have difficulty leaving.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Tunisia entry requirements

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read makes insurance a condition of entry for visa-exempt tourists. The UK government advises travel insurance for local treatment or unexpected medical evacuation: there is no free medical attention for foreign nationals, and doctors' fees, medication and treatment in private clinics must be paid on the spot.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Tunisia travel advice (health)

onwardTicket.text: No official source we could read requires a return or onward ticket. The UK FCDO says border officials have the right to ask on arrival for your onward or return travel tickets, and that a small number of visitors have been denied entry or delayed for not being able to provide sufficient evidence of accommodation.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Tunisia travel advice (entry requirements)

proofOfFunds.text: No official source we could read states a proof-of-funds requirement or amount for Tunisia. The UK Foreign Office lists what border officials have the right to ask for on arrival, including proof of a hotel booking or other accommodation details; funds are not on its list.

currencyLimits.text: Tunisian Customs says any import or export of foreign currency worth 20,000 Tunisian dinars or more must be declared to Customs on entry, on exit and in transit. A non-resident can re-export more than 5,000 dinars' worth of the foreign banknotes they brought in only if they declared them on entry, and not more than 30,000 dinars' worth (above that, through authorised banks and financial institutions); the import declaration is valid for 3 months from entry and for one trip only. Keep the exchange slip when you change currency into dinars: you will need it to change leftover dinars back at a bank.

safety.text: The UK FCDO advises against all travel to parts of western Tunisia, including the Chaambi Mountains National Park and designated military operations zones, and to parts of the south along the Libyan border, due to cross-border terrorist activity and fighting in Libya. The Government of Canada says a state of emergency has been in effect since 2015 and is regularly extended due to the threat of terrorism.

bestTimeToVisit.text: No official source we could read gives a best time to visit. The Government of Canada says that in the north summers are hot and dry and winters are rainy, and that between June and September temperatures can exceed 40°C and sand and dust storms are frequent.

idp.text: Tunisia is a party to the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic (UN Treaty Collection). The UK government says British drivers can drive in Tunisia for up to one year with a 1968 international driving permit (IDP) and their UK driving licence, and also need to carry a green card to prove they have the minimum insurance cover. Canada's travel advice says Canadians can drive in Tunisia with a valid Canadian driver's licence and should have an International Driving Permit. The UK government says the legal drink-driving limit in Tunisia is stricter than for England and Wales. No official source we could read states Tunisia's own rule for drivers holding a foreign licence.

tips.text: The Government of Canada says importing and exporting Tunisian dinars is prohibited. The UK FCDO says to keep official exchange receipts.

The UK Foreign Office says that if you overstay the 90-day period without a valid reason you will have to pay a fine, which you can pay on departure at the airport or in advance at some police stations. The Government of Canada says to contact a Tunisian embassy or consulate before departure if you wish to stay more than 90 days.

The UK FCDO advises against all travel to the Chaambi Mountains National Park, the designated military operations zones, and parts of the Tunisia-Libya border area. The Government of Canada advises avoiding all travel to fenced-off military zones such as the area south of Remada, in Tataouine governorate.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Tunisia?
faq.answer: Tunisia's Foreign Ministry visa-regime table marks no entry visa for citizens of countries including Germany, the UK, the US, Canada, Japan, Argentina, Brazil and Chile, marks one for others such as Cyprus, and says the visa principle applies to every country not on the list.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Tunisia without a visa?
faq.answer: The Foreign Ministry's visa table states no length of stay. The Government of Canada says that to stay more than 90 days you should contact the nearest Tunisian embassy or consulate before your departure. The UK Foreign Office says that if you overstay the 90-day period without a valid reason you will have to pay a fine, which you can pay on departure at the airport or in advance at some police stations.

faq.question: Can I bring Tunisian dinars in or out of the country?
faq.answer: The Government of Canada says importing and exporting Tunisian dinars is prohibited, and the UK FCDO says you are not allowed to take Tunisian dinars out of Tunisia and to keep official exchange receipts. Tunisian Customs says any import or export of foreign currency worth 20,000 Tunisian dinars or more must be declared to Customs on entry, on exit and in transit.

faq.question: Can Israeli citizens visit Tunisia?
faq.answer: Tunisia's Foreign Ministry visa-regime table does not list Israel, and says the visa requirement applies to every country not on the list. No official source we could read states whether Israeli passport holders are admitted.

faq.question: Is Tunisia safe for tourists?
faq.answer: The UK FCDO advises against all travel to parts of western Tunisia, including the Chaambi Mountains National Park and designated military operations zones, and to parts of the south along the Libyan border, including the militarised zone south of El Borma and Dhehiba and the town of Ben Guerdane. The Government of Canada says a state of emergency has been in effect since 2015 because of the threat of terrorism.

faq.question: Do I need a return ticket to enter Tunisia?
faq.answer: The UK FCDO says border officials have the right to ask on arrival for your onward or return travel tickets and proof of a hotel booking or other accommodation details, and that a small number of visitors have been denied entry or delayed for not being able to provide sufficient evidence of accommodation.

Les voyageurs non-résidents ne peuvent pas réexporter la contre-valeur d’un montant qui dépasse trente mille (30.000) dinars des devises en billets de banques qu’ils ont importés et déclarés à l’entrée.
En cas de dépassement du dit montant, la réexportation doit être réalisée par les établissements financiers et bancaires habilités
La déclaration d’importation de devises est valable pour (3) mois à compter de la date d’entrée du voyageur non résident en Tunisie et ne peut servir, en tout état de cause, que pour un seul voyage.

En cas d’échange de devises contre des dinars, conservez le bordereau de change. Ce document vous sera utile lorsque vous voudrez échanger, auprès d’une banque, le reliquat des dinars en votre possession contre des devises.
